title: Read the 31 unread club depth charts, one page each
why: This single task unblocks the deficiency matrix, the injury ablation, the per-team replacement view and the depth-of-replacement column at the same time. Today the desk can name a replacement for one club.
risk: Low. The schema already stores the club string verbatim and marks a club NOT READ, so nothing has to be redesigned.

title: Capture the inactive list inside each game's own pre-kickoff window
why: Turns Questionable from a word into a measured play rate, and confirms whether a named replacement actually played.
risk: Medium. The window is narrow and a missed read cannot be recreated; the desk would have to log the miss as a miss.

title: Settle Week 11 and start the leaderboard clock
why: Every competition question here is unanswerable without settled bets, and the sample needed is 4,721 bets, so the clock should start as soon as possible if the competition is real.
effort: One graded results pass per week
risk: Low, provided every bet carries the pre-kickoff capture id it was priced from.

title: Ask the operators in writing whether a scheduled read is permitted
why: The whole price store is a manual read because the terms of the two operator boards were not verifiable from this sandbox. A written answer converts a manual chore into a monitor, or confirms it stays manual.
risk: None to the site; the answer may be no, in which case nothing changes.

title: Publish a season-by-season home-edge series
why: The solved home edge is +1.17 on the two-season window against roughly 2.2 historically, and -0.56 on a 2026-only fit. One table settles whether that is a real shift or an artefact of the window.
risk: Low. It changes no price; it stops a small home edge being explained away.

title: Show the fair line as a price, not only as a number
why: A line of -6.5 is not tradeable; the price that would make it worth taking is. The desk already converts to American prices on the moneyline rows and could do the same for side and total.
risk: Low, but it must not become a bet recommendation. The site should show what price would be needed, never tell anyone to take one.

title: Add a market-favourite control column to the leaderboard
why: A favourites-only control is already registered (C2); showing it beside each strategy makes it obvious when a strategy is just following the market.
risk: None. It can only make a weak strategy look weaker.

title: Consolidate the duplicate desks in this repository
why: More than forty NFL desks publish overlapping Week 11 numbers with different market columns. A reader cannot tell which is current. This desk should either absorb them or be archived alongside them.
effort: An owner decision, then one integration pass
risk: Medium. Removing a desk that holds the only verified copy of something would lose it, so it should be archived, not deleted.

title: Freeze this registration in a signed tag before Week 12
why: A sha256 inside a file can be recomputed by anyone who edits the file. A git tag is harder to rewrite and is the registration the brief asks for.

title: Add a liveness badge to every captured number
why: A price read eight hours ago and a price read eight days ago look identical on the page. A badge that says how old the read is stops a stale number being mistaken for a current one.
